title: Install an old-work electrical box in a drywall cut-out and drive both swing-clamp screws until it is held tight
instruction: Install the blue electrical box in the hole in the wall: push it in until its ears are flat on the wall, then drive both of its clamp screws with the screwdriver until the box is held tight. Put the screwdriver down and take both hands away.
context: Electricians (O*NET 47-2111.00, 821,000 US jobs in 2025) have the Core task "Fasten small metal or plastic boxes to walls to house electrical switches or outlets." A box goes on a stud before the drywall is hung; in a finished wall it is an old-work box clamped to the drywall, so nearly every switch or outlet added in an existing building, the work of service and remodel electricians and of general maintenance workers (49-9071.00, 1.6 million), uses one. Maker's steps: "Trace Box, Cut on Lines, Insert Wires, Place Box in Wall, Secure Box in Wall"; this task is the last two, without the cable (see fidelity). The hard part is physical: the box goes square into a cut-out 1.6 mm wider than it each side until both ears are flat; each clamp screw is driven horizontally with a #2 Phillips tip pressed into a 1.8 mm recess, in wrist strokes; and the clamps are hidden behind the board, so the only sign one has gripped is the screw stalling.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. 1) Wall section (fixed; its bottom plate clamped to the table): 1/2 in (12.7 mm) gypsum drywall, 480 wide and 400 tall, its face at x 340 facing the arms, centred on y 0, fixed to a 2x4 (38 x 89 mm) pine bottom plate and top plate and two 2x4 studs 16 in (406 mm) on centre at y +-203; the back of the stud bay is open. In the drywall, centred on y 0 and 190 up, a 1-gang cut-out made from the box's template: 2-1/4 x 3-5/8 in (57.2 wide, 92.1 tall). 2) Box: a blue PVC 1-gang old-work box with mounting ears and two swing clamps (for example a Carlon B114R: 4-1/8 L x 2-1/4 W x 2-3/4 D in, 14 cu in, 56.7 g). Its front rim and ears (2.5 mm thick, 57 x 104.8 mm) bear on the wall 6.4 mm above and below the cut-out; the body behind them is 54 x 89 mm at the ears and 50 x 85 mm at the back (moulding draft), with 2.5 mm walls. Two clamp screws (7.4 mm pan heads, #2 Phillips) on its centre line 37 mm above and below its middle, heads on the ears' face. Each drives a white plastic clamp arm (19 mm from the screw's axis, 7 wide, 3 thick), delivered folded inside the box 24 mm behind the ears: turned clockwise, the screw swings it out through a slot in the box's end wall to its stop, then draws it toward the ears onto the back of the drywall (in the simulation about 3.4 turns from folded to clamped; see fidelity). No cable. The box lies on its back on the table, open face up, its long side along x, centred at x 200, y 170. 3) Screwdriver: a #2 Phillips stubby, 92 mm overall (6 mm shaft 42 mm long, red and yellow octagonal handle 30 mm across flats, 50 mm long), 50 g, standing tip down in its block with the cross of its tip along x and y. 4) Block: beech, 50 x 50 x 44 mm tall, with a 10 mm square hole through it, fixed to the table centred at x 170, y -170; the screwdriver's shaft is in the hole and its handle rests on the block. Both arms start at their ready poses, grippers open. Nothing else is on the table; the layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read every control step; the score is the last step's. Flush: the box's centre within 2 mm of the cut-out's centre, and each ear's back face within 0.5 mm of the wall at both its corners. A clamp is tight when its arm has swung out 80 degrees or more (90 at its stop) and presses the back of the drywall with 20 N or more, and its screw has turned no more than 0.25 turn without the screwdriver in it (in it: the tip in the recess's cross, within 2.5 mm of the screw's axis, the shaft within 25 degrees of the axis). Put down: the screwdriver's lowest point within 5 cm of the table top (on the table or in its block), not in a screw. Hands off: every point of both grippers 3 cm or more from the box and from the screwdriver. Still: the box and the screwdriver each moved 1 mm or less over the last 1 s. 1.0: flush, both clamps tight, screwdriver put down, hands off and still, all held for 1 s (20 steps), which ends the trial. 0.75: flush and both clamps tight. 0.5: flush and one clamp tight. 0.25: the box was flush at some point. Else 0. Real trial: the wall section's back is open, so after the trial each arm is checked from behind (swung out over the board, a 0.1 mm feeler will not pass under it); tight also means a further quarter turn with the screwdriver takes force, and the box moves 0.5 mm or less (feeler gauge) when pulled straight out with 20 N on a luggage scale hooked over its rim; ear gaps with a 0.5 mm feeler gauge; that each screw was turned only with the screwdriver, from the video.
reset_notes: Back both clamp screws out (counter-clockwise) until each arm has swung back into the box and stops, 24 mm behind the ears; pull the box out and lay it on its back at its marks. Stand the screwdriver in its block, its tip's cross along and across the table. Replace the drywall panel when the cut-out's edges or the board behind the clamps show crushing (each install presses the board's back with the clamps).
fidelity: CPU PhysX, rigid bodies. Each clamp: a screw, a threaded hub (thread = PhysX mimic joint) and an arm on a 40 N/mm spring (its bending); thread friction swings the arm out, a contact stops it, and it clamps by contact. Thread 4 mm/turn (real ~0.8): 3.4 turns, not ~15. Gypsum is rigid (no crushing). The cable, fed in before the box goes in, is left out. Frictions, spring, 20 N: estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (6,000 steps; never put the box in the cut-out); scripted demo: 1.0 (success at step 4,119)
